title: Counters: CTU, CTD and CTUD
oneLiner: Up, down and up/down counters: they count rising edges, not scans; reset and load take priority; and the outputs flag when a preset is reached.
keyTakeaway: CTU counts CU edges up from 0 (R clears it, Q = CV >= PV); CTD counts CD edges down from PV (LD loads it, Q = CV <= 0); CTUD does both. Decide deliberately whether a count must survive a power cut.
explanation:
Counters are function blocks that count rising edges, so a part sitting in front of a sensor counts once, not once per scan. The up counter CTU adds one to its current value CV on each rising edge of its CU input, is cleared by its reset input R, and sets its output Q once CV reaches the preset value PV. The down counter CTD loads PV when its LD input is TRUE and counts down on CD edges, setting Q when it reaches zero. The up/down counter CTUD combines both, which suits anything that goes in and comes out again, such as parts in a buffer zone.

Typical uses are batch counts (a box every 10 parts), production totals, cycle counts for maintenance, and tracking how many items are between two sensors. The details worth knowing are which input wins when several are active at once, what happens at the limits of the count, and whether the count survives a power cut.
